verdict.rationale: Plaid documents Link as the single client-side component users go through so you can access their accounts via the API, and separately documents Auth, Balance, Transactions and Identity. The Sandbox endpoint takes plural "initial products" for one Item, and a community user reports that a single Plaid flow exposes transaction data, identity and real-time balance together. Still, no first-party doc explicitly says one Link session initializes multiple products. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of configuring multiple products in one Link token/session, details on adding products to an existing Item without relinking, and hands-on developer corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, one link session can power multiple data products — auth, balances, transactions, identity — without forcing the user through separate connection flows per product

citations.quote: Plaid Link is the client-side component that your users will interact with in order to link their accounts to Plaid and allow you to access their accounts via the Plaid API.
This endpoint allows you to generate a public_token for an arbitrary institution ID, initial products, and test credentials.
when you go through a Plaid flow that you're likely giving away much more than just the bare minimum account numbers... transaction data, identity, real-time balance, etc.
